stories.headline: Plugin4Shell: zero-click RCE across Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, and Gemini CLI
stories.why_read: Still the keys-to-the-kingdom agent supply-chain beat — Copilot unpatched, Gemini CLI retiring.
body: Air Security's Plugin4Shell disclosure still dominates the coding-agent desk: marketplace plugins can be swapped upstream when Git treats a pinned SHA as a branch name, and auto-updating agents turn that into zero-click remote code execution across Anthropic's Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Google's Gemini CLI.

Anthropic reportedly patched in Claude Code 2.1.179 and OpenAI in Codex 0.146.0; Copilot still lacked a fix in Air's accounting, and Gemini CLI is being retired toward Antigravity rather than patched. Update the harness, then treat plugin marketplaces like untrusted CI.

stories.headline: Android 17: first since 3.x to ship new APIs without releasing them to AOSP
stories.why_read: HN ~951 pts — GrapheneOS flags a watershed break in Android's open-source contract.
body: GrapheneOS reported that Android 17 is the first release since the 3.x era to add new APIs without publishing them to the Android Open Source Project. Hacker News piled higher (~951 points, 500+ comments) around what that means for OEM forks, privacy builds, and the long-assumed AOSP commons.

Systems story more than phone-review story: if platform surfaces stay proprietary, the open Android that GrapheneOS and others rebuild becomes a second-class citizen. Watch how Google frames the split — and what device makers do next.

stories.headline: Texas Robotaxi hits 448 vehicles — Cybercab roster climbs to 58
stories.why_read: Anand RTd the live tracker: +9 Cybercabs on Sep 18; TxDMV now shows 390 Model Y + 58 Cybercab.
body: Public Texas automated-vehicle records mirrored by TeslaNorth and Texas AV Tracker show Tesla Robotaxi's authorized fleet at 448 after nine more Cybercab VINs stamped September 18 — lifting purpose-built Cybercabs from 49 earlier in the month to 58, beside 390 Model Y robotaxis.

Registration is not the same as paid rides in Austin's geofence, but it is the clearest hard metric that Tesla is still feeding production Cybercabs into the commercial pipeline. Hold beside NHTSA's sworn FMVSS Special Order due September 30.

stories.headline: Grok Bots grow webhooks — trigger agents from any platform
stories.why_read: Anand RTd mattyp: ask your bot how to set up webhooks; SpaceX CFO says Grok Bot is exploding.
body: Matt Palmer's note that Grok Bots support webhooks — so they can be triggered from any platform — landed in Anand's RT stream with a simple onboarding path: ask the bot how to set them up. That turns X-native agents into event-driven workers instead of chat-only toys.
It pairs with a SpaceX CFO clip Anand also amplified: Grok progressing faster than competitors while Grok Bot grows faster than anything the company has seen. Agent surface area is the product now.

stories.headline: Laya: open-source System-1 decision engine answering the Jev wave
stories.why_read: HN ~365 pts — sub-35ms typed decisions, Apache-2 weights, and a direct challenge to TypeSafe's closed Jev.
body: ConvAI Innovations' Laya Show HN pitches a non-autoregressive decision model family: choice/score/boolean primitives, ~33 ms latency on commodity GPUs, multilingual routing, and Apache-2.0 weights — framed explicitly as an open answer after TypeSafe AI's Jev launch.

Anand's bookmark shelf is thick with Jev explainers (harness essays, Vercel AI Gateway, Aaron Levie). Laya makes the same bet local and OSS: keep frontier LLMs for hard thinking; use a fast typed classifier for route/score/stop.

stories.headline: Claude Code now reads AGENTS.md when CLAUDE.md is missing
stories.why_read: HN ~691 pts — harness conventions converge; one agents file to rule the desk.
body: Anthropic's Claude Code changelog notes that the tool now reads AGENTS.md if there is no CLAUDE.md. Hacker News celebrated (~691 points): the industry is slowly agreeing that agent instructions belong in a portable, repo-local file instead of a vendor-shaped one.
Practical desk news next to Plugin4Shell on the same fold — standardize the harness file, then harden how plugins land.

stories.headline: Microsoft exec called AI scraping 'the largest theft of labor in human history'
stories.why_read: Now ~905 pts — the quote that keeps climbing on a Saturday.
body: TechCrunch's unredacted-filings story — a Microsoft executive describing AI scraping as the largest theft of labor in human history — kept climbing on Hacker News (now ~905 points). The labor-vs-scale tension is still the cleanest articulation of the week's policy fight.
Copyright, training data, and who gets paid when models learn — still the clearest policy shelf on an otherwise agent-and-fleet Saturday.

stories.headline: Cloudflare Quick Tunnels — one command, public encrypted URL, no account
stories.why_read: HN ~766 pts and Anand RTd Nick Gray: laptop server to edge URL without the ceremony.
body: Cloudflare's Quick Tunnels (try.cloudflare.com) surged on Hacker News (~766 points) as the path of least resistance for exposing a local service behind a temporary public hostname. Anand amplified Nick Gray's framing: one command, no account, no DNS, no open ports.
For agent demos and weekend hacks, tunnel latency beats waiting on a full Zero Trust setup — companion systems energy to the 100TB RAM post.

stories.headline: Building a Harness with Jev — the X article Anand bookmarked hard
stories.why_read: Sydney Runkle's harness essay + Vercel AI Gateway availability; Anand saved both.
body: Sydney Runkle's X article 'Building a Harness with Jev' is the practical how-to Anand bookmarked alongside a thick Jev explainers shelf — classifiers that pick from options instead of generating text, wired into agent loops for route/score/stop decisions.
Vercel already ships TypeSafe's Jev on AI Gateway via an experimental evaluate API. Read next to Laya and OpenJev: the harness layer is converging whether you buy the API or run open weights.

stories.headline: Meta Muse: Peter Yang's favorite personal agent — and it negotiated his bills
stories.why_read: Anand RTd Yang: free agent that saved $800+/yr on cable and phone via real phone calls.
body: Peter Yang called Meta's Muse the best personal agent he has tried — citing real savings of $800+ a year after Muse called customer support and renegotiated cable and phone bills, plus morning briefings and habit tracking.
Consumer agents that act in the world (not just chat) are the same product thesis as Grok Bots webhooks and enterprise Jev harnesses — different shelf, same 'does it ship outcomes' test.

stories.headline: TFR over SpaceX McGregor — Roadster launch event eyed for October 1
stories.why_read: Anand RTd Joe Tegtmeyer: unique Tesla/SpaceX flight restriction near Waco through Oct 2.
body: Joe Tegtmeyer flagged a Temporary Flight Restriction over SpaceX's McGregor test facility near Waco — up to 10,000 feet, ~1.5-mile radius, running through October 2 — and tied it to a October 1 Roadster launch-event unveiling rather than a routine static fire.
Whether the show is a hop, a demo, or theater, the airspace paperwork is real. Tesla product calendar energy beside Cybercab fleet growth and the NHTSA clock.

stories.headline: Top Gear tours the Tesla Semi factory — 'most significant Tesla since Model 3'
stories.why_read: Anand RTd tesla_semi: 1.7 kWh/mi vs diesel at ~3× the energy for comparable work.
body: A Top Gear factory tour and ride in a production Tesla Semi with Dan Priestley framed the truck as possibly the most significant Tesla since the Model 3. The energy punchline Anand amplified: ~1.7 kWh/mi — about 7× a Model Y's energy at ~20× the weight — while a comparable diesel uses roughly 3× as much energy as the Semi.
Energy + IT taste map in one clip: freight electrification is still a systems problem measured in kilowatt-hours per mile, not just range anxiety slides.

stories.headline: Disney names Karandeep Anand its first-ever chief technology officer
stories.why_read: Anand RTd Bloomberg: AI executive into a newly created entertainment-giant CTO seat.
body: Walt Disney Co. named Karandeep Anand to a newly created chief technology officer role — Bloomberg framed it as installing an AI-fluent executive as the entertainment giant's first-ever CTO.
IT-architecture shelf for a Saturday otherwise heavy on agents and fleets: big media is still hiring the person who owns the tech stack when every product roadmap says 'AI'.

stories.headline: SpaceX CFO: Grok progressing fastest; Grok Bot growing faster than anything seen
stories.why_read: Anand RTd the clip — internal growth framing for the same bots now shipping webhooks.
body: A widely shared clip Anand amplified quotes SpaceX's CFO saying Grok is progressing faster than any competitor while Grok Bot is growing faster than anything the company has seen. Treat corporate boosterism carefully; treat the product surface seriously.
Together with webhook triggers and Uncle Bob-style 'prompt every ten minutes' workflows, the Grok agent desk is no longer a side quest — it is a primary beat for Anand's X taste map.

stories.headline: US military close call after AI hallucinated an intelligence report
stories.why_read: HN ~477 pts — CNN: false AI intel on a China ship nearly drove a bad call.
body: CNN reported a US military close call after an AI system produced a hallucinated intelligence report involving a Chinese ship. The thread on Hacker News (~477 points) is less dunk and more systems-failure autopsy: verification loops, human review, and what 'AI-assisted intel' actually means under time pressure.
Pairs with yesterday's agent-security wave — when models write the brief, the harness that checks the brief is the product.

stories.headline: Researchers used Anthropic's Claude to help breach OpenAI — $6,500 bounty
stories.why_read: TechCrunch + Anand bookmarked Deedy's note on the three Indian researchers behind it.
body: Hacktron AI researchers, working through OpenAI's bug-bounty program, used Anthropic's Claude (ultimately Opus-class) while chaining flaws that led to takeover of OpenAI employee ChatGPT/Codex accounts and demonstrated GitHub organization access via a harmless PR. OpenAI paid a $6,500 bounty; researchers say they did not view source.

Anand bookmarked Deedy's shout-out to Rahul Maini, Mohan Pedhapati, and Harsh Jaiswal — curiosity and skill over brand-name credentials. Update the mental model: agent coding security is both Plugin4Shell and Claude-in-the-red-team.

stories.headline: OpenJev still climbing — typed millisecond decisions vs frontier chat
stories.why_read: HN ~658 pts — keep Jev context beside today's Laya and harness bookmarks.
body: OpenJev remains high on HN (~658 points) as the public face of TypeSafe's Jev decision-model wave: keep frontier LLMs for hard thinking; use a typed, millisecond classifier for route/score/stop decisions.
Essential context beside Laya's OSS answer and Anand's harness bookmarks — harness semantics over vibes.

stories.headline: Starship Flight 14 locked to ~Sep 28 — first orbit + 26 Starlink V3 still the goal
stories.why_read: SpaceX slipped from Sep 22; India Today/TeslaNorth confirm Monday NET pending approval.
body: SpaceX is now targeting Starship Flight 14 as early as Monday, September 28, pending regulatory approval — a roughly six-day slip from the prior September 22 window. The public profile still aims at Starship's first orbital attempt (~275 km, about six orbits) with 26 Starlink V3 satellites and Super Heavy recovery offshore in the Gulf.
Keep Construction Physics' Raptor manufacturing essay beside the countdown: cadence and engine learning curves are what turn a spectacular test into a reusable logistics system.

stories.headline: NHTSA Special Order: Tesla must prove Cybercab is legal to sell — under oath by Sep 30
stories.why_read: Sworn FMVSS clock still ticking while Texas Cybercab roster hits 58.
body: Electrek reported NHTSA's formal Special Order requiring Tesla to answer detailed questions under oath by September 30 about how a wheel-, pedal-, and mirror-free Cybercab complies with FMVSS written for human drivers. The order escalates the Audit Query opened as commercial Austin service began.
Hold next to today's fleet featured: delight, first-responder process, and sworn compliance are still different chapters.

stories.headline: Stanford Medicine: the human brain behaves like two separate organs
stories.why_read: HN ~441 pts — developmental biology that reframes 'one brain' intuition.
body: Stanford Medicine-led research argues the human brain is better understood as two separate organs in developmental and functional terms, echoing companion coverage that two parallel neural ectoderm progenitors contributed to the developing brain. Hacker News (~441 points) did the weekend science deep-dive.
Physics/Chem/Math-adjacent kindness on the pinned taste map — pure curiosity between agent CVEs.

stories.headline: Terry Tao: if math is more than proof, celebrate the rest of it
stories.why_read: Fresh Tao blog post on HN — exploration, intuition, and exposition as first-class math.
body: Terence Tao's September 18 post argues that if mathematics is more than formal proof, the community should better celebrate exploration, intuition, exposition, and the other crafts that make proofs possible. Hacker News amplified it into a Saturday morning seminar.
Love/Laughter/Kindness amplifiers include making hard ideas hospitable — Tao's beat lands squarely on Anand's pinned map.

stories.headline: I don't like passkeys — the HN identity-wars reopen
stories.why_read: HN ~799 pts — recovery, platform lock-in, and UX friction in one rant that stuck.
body: Hawksley's 'I don't like passkeys' essay detonated on Hacker News (~799 points). Whatever you think of WebAuthn, the comments are a useful catalog of recovery nightmares, platform gating, and the gap between security theory and family-tech support calls.
Identity shelf for a week otherwise dominated by agent CVEs — auth UX is still infrastructure.

stories.headline: Hister: private search over the pages you visit and the files you keep
stories.why_read: HN ~713 pts — local index for tabs, PDFs, and agent droppings.
body: Hister (GitHub) remains a top private-search story on HN (~713 points): index browsing history and local files without shipping them to a cloud RAG vendor. In an agent-heavy desk, retrieval over what you already saw is underrated infrastructure.
Systems holdover that still fits Saturday — put search where the work already is.

stories.headline: Bend: a language that blocks AI mistakes via proof — on CPU and GPU
stories.why_read: HN ~601 pts — typed/proofed agent output instead of vibes-only codegen.
body: Bend's landing page and HN thread (~601 points) still pitch proofs that block AI mistakes while targeting CPU and GPU. Companion posts on Bend 2 and the 'vibe-coding trap' keep the debate warm.
If agents write the bulk of the code, the substrate that rejects nonsense becomes the product — still true on day two.

stories.headline: Bonsai 2 27B: near-lossless compression in a 9x smaller footprint
stories.why_read: HN ~571 pts — LocalLLaMA-grade efficiency without the usual quality cliff.
body: PrismML's Bonsai 2 27B write-up still holds (~571 HN points) with near-lossless compression into a roughly 9x smaller footprint. For intelligence-per-watt hunters, compression that preserves quality beats another tiny chat model.
Pairs with Laya on today's fold: the local-inference frontier remains a systems contest.

stories.headline: How to Write with an LLM — craft advice that treats the model as collaborator
stories.why_read: HN ~546 pts — editing discipline over prompt cosplay.
body: Sockpuppet's How to Write with an LLM (~546 HN points) remains the practical craft essay for people already living in Claude/Codex/Grok loops. The useful stance: the model drafts; you still own voice, structure, and truth.
Saturday holdover for the agent-desk crowd — human judgment checklists still matter.

stories.headline: Cloudflare: saving another 100TB of RAM — with math
stories.why_read: HN ~406 pts — fleet memory as a first-class product surface.
body: Cloudflare's follow-up on saving another 100TB of RAM via careful data-structure and math work hit Hacker News (~406 points). It is the rare infra post that reads like a performance thriller without a new product launch attached.
Systems craft for anyone running agent sidecars and edge fleets: RAM still has a price tag even when GPUs steal the headlines.

stories.headline: How SpaceX streamlined the Raptor engine — Construction Physics deep dive
stories.why_read: Holdover — manufacturing cadence behind the F14 orbital attempt.
body: Construction Physics' essay on how SpaceX streamlined Raptor still sits next to Flight 14's slipped orbital window. Fewer parts, faster builds, and production learning curves are what separate demo flights from cadence.
Space systems holdover: engine architecture remains a competitive sport.

stories.headline: First new cat species discovered in 100 years
stories.why_read: HN ~311 pts — National Geographic weekend delight.
body: National Geographic's report on the first new cat species discovered in a century climbed Hacker News (~311 points). Pure animal-science palate cleanser after a week of agent CVEs and FMVSS oaths.
Love/Laughter/Kindness shelf — curiosity without a product roadmap.

stories.headline: You only get one summer with your baby — the parenting reminder Anand RTd
stories.why_read: Anand amplified theficouple: finite summers with each stage of childhood.
body: A widely shared parenting note Anand retweeted lists the finite summers you get with a baby, toddler, child, and teenager — and asks young parents not to rush them. Soft signal on a hard-news fold.
Love/Laughter/Kindness amplifier exactly as pinned: keep the human calendar visible between fleets, agents, and orbital slips.
